summary: Measured the R9700 ceilings (WMMA issue peak 194 bf16 / 377 fp8 TFLOPS; hipBLASLt ~170 / ~300 at prefill shapes) and a per-class roofline of main's 35B prefill: the GDN scan is the largest class (24.6 % at 4k), routed experts run at 36-46 % of a dense-GEMM ideal but 1.8x per-expert hipBLASLt, fp8 dense at 58 % of hipBLASLt fp8. Shipped three bitwise changes (GDN scan v3 rescheduled, gdn.hip in CU mode, 16-wave f8 prefill tiles): localeval prefill +4.2 % at 4k (9327 -> 9703) and +4.6 % at 16k (8445 -> 8834), decode unchanged, ids identical. PR #115 is a draft because qualify quick exits 2 on main and lane alike (ref_noise sidecar / golden hash mismatch on tatooine).
lessons: The GDN delta-rule scan is bound by its per-token LDS reads of q/k plus the latency chain: removing the LDS reads halves it (0.32 us/token/layer), and CU mode alone is -13 %.

One-lane-per-row scan variants (128 state registers per lane: v3r, DPP broadcast v4/v6-v8, scalar-load v5) all spill on gfx12 and are 1.4-7x slower; hipcc does not fold a DPP move into v_fmac (inline asm v_fmac_f32_dpp works but still spills).
The fp32 SIMT chunked (WY) GDN that won on GB10 is slower than the sequential scan on gfx1201 (1.10 vs 0.71 us/token at T=4096); a WY port needs WMMA (numerics change).

Routed experts already beat per-expert hipBLASLt by 1.8x at the real ~128 pairs/expert; the next big lever there is a W4A8 path on the fp8 WMMA (e2m1 exact in e4m3, one NVFP4 scale block = one fp8 WMMA K of 16).
f8 tiles: the 128x256 tile underfills the GPU at small N (k/v, M 2049: +56 %), so it is gated on >= 64 blocks; any tile gives the same bits because the k order does not depend on the tile.
qualify on tatooine currently cannot PASS for the 35B: repo golden/ref_noise sidecar was measured on a different golden hash than /data/models/intarsia/golden.
Many 15-s GPU windows in a row (w3-w8) break the 5-min gap rule; batch microbenchmarks into one window.
